gate_clause_verbatim: Records: the W11 change records; N is the count in the change log, 1 expected. Lanes: two blind non-author lanes with different briefs (the OW-19 floor), neither of them the W9, W10 or W11 author, on the same pinned layers (the installed FIXUP-9 rows, the FIXUP-10 applied rows, OSHB, WEB, the mark layer, the device inventory). Each packet holds exactly N items, each with a verdict of support or challenge, a grade (low, medium or high) for a challenge, asks_row_change true or false, and the bytes read. Each lane answers three ordered checks, yes or no, with the bytes read: after_text_equal (in W4-004 boundary_evidence_refs entry 1 the E12 after text has count 1 and the E12 before text count 0); w4_004_device_words_match_pattern (by the lane's own script, oshb Dan.7.14 has the word count the entry gives, and the inventory pattern of everlasting_dominion_aram, searched over the mark-stripped words of that verse, matches exactly the words the entry gives); w4_004_entry_agrees_with_row (the entry does not contradict W4-004 boundary_rationale or the mark layer at Dan.7.14). Closed, and peers met, when: both packets hold N items; 0 challenges are graded medium or high; 0 items ask a row change; 0 extra findings in either packet are graded medium or high or ask a row change; all three ordered checks are answered yes in both packets; and B1 to B12 and B14 to B16, as E12 amends them, pass by script on the FIXUP-10 applied file. The orchestrator then records peers met and the boss may launch without another controlling ruling. Any other outcome returns to the controlling agent.

text.what: The entry's unchanged words 'in the closing verse of the vision report' are a reading in a field that takes no tier word. The bytes I read are consistent with it (PE after Dan.7.14; oshb Dan.7.15 opens אֶתְכְּרִיַּ֥ת רוּחִ֛י אֲנָ֥ה דָנִיֵּ֖אל, the seer's reaction) but do not decide it; FIXUP-10 did not change these words and E12 left the reading to the end review.
text.why_it_matters: It is the basis the entry gives for the far side of the onset; a script cannot settle it.

text.what: The unchanged boundary_rationale says the key 'is listed' at the dominion clause of words 12 to 14, while the pattern match is words 13 to 14. I read 'where' as the clause that contains the key's words, which the bytes support; a stricter reader could take it as the extent of the key. E12 ordered these words to stay.
text.why_it_matters: If read as the key's extent it would repeat, in the rationale, the one-word imprecision E12 corrected in the entry.

text.what: The inventory pattern is not anchored to word boundaries; I counted a match by the words it overlaps and confirmed that the one match begins and ends on word boundaries.
text.why_it_matters: With a different inventory pattern an overlap count and a whole-word count could differ; here they are the same.

text.what: Every lane and the ruling ran on one model family, a recorded downgrade and not an equivalence; my support rests on the script output only.
text.why_it_matters: Agreement between lanes is not independent confirmation.

text.what: Both lanes, the author and the ruling run on one model family as a recorded fallback; this packet's support rests on its own script output, not on the ruling's printed output.
text.why_it_matters: Agreement between lanes is one voice; the end review still owes its own look at the ruling.

text.what: Whether oshb Dan.7.14 is rightly called 'the closing verse of the vision report' is a reading the change did not touch; I checked only that it is coherent with W4-003 ending on 7:14 as a dream_or_vision_report and with the strategy's example 7:2-7:14.
text.why_it_matters: E12 leaves that reading to the end review; this packet does not confirm it.

text.what: The entry's word range now names the two words of the inventory pattern's match, while W4-003 quotes three words (with the suffixed noun at word 12) beside the same key without a position, and W4-004 boundary_rationale speaks of 'the dominion clause at words 12 to 14'. I judge these consistent (the clause contains the match), not contradictory; a reader could wish the fields used one convention.
text.why_it_matters: It is a wording difference in unchanged text, not a false claim; raised for the end review only, and not as a finding.

text.what: The hygiene scan uses my own word lists for model names, ruling ids and process talk; the lists are not a pinned definition.
text.why_it_matters: A term outside my lists would not be caught by the scan, though I also read the entry in full and saw none.

text.what: I did not run the validator suite or the B1 to B16 gate measures; they are not among my pinned inputs.
text.why_it_matters: The gate's script conditions on the applied file are the orchestrator's to measure, not shown by this packet.

tier: MEASURED for the counts, digests and script conditions (this script); REPORTED for the content of each lane's findings, which is TRANSCRIBED into the carried list
limits: both lanes and the author ran on one model family under the recorded fallback (OW-25); agreement between lanes is not independent confirmation
the script counts verdicts, grades, cured flags and row-change flags; it does not judge any finding
